plan.title: docs(scm): merge queue setup playbook, and point agents to it where they merge

narratives.Description: Master runs a GitHub merge queue since 2026-11-16, but nothing tells an agent or a consumer how to turn one on. This story adds a setup playbook at content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md and points agents to it where they merge: scm/github.md § Merge queue mode, the review-cycle merge step, and one advisory line from pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge on a strict branch with no queue. Operator additions fold in a Known issues and a Saving rounds section in the playbook, and one pointer in the consumer AGENTS.md template and the swarm skill to run swarm:pre-dispatch begin before any implementation worker (#6379).
narratives.UserStory: As a maintainer or agent on a repository with strict up-to-date checks, I want one playbook that sets up and explains the merge queue, so that every merge stops putting every open PR behind.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Add content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md (drafted by the parent), checked against master at 0.129.11, plus the Known issues and Saving rounds sections.
2. Link it from content/scm/github.md § Merge queue mode and from the review-cycle merge step through content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json, then task packs:render.
3. In packages/core/src/pr-wait-mergeable: detectStrictUpToDate and mergeQueueAdvisoryLine in merge-queue.ts, printed on the direct path from cascade.ts, exported from index.ts; tests in merge-queue.test.ts.
4. Add the swarm:pre-dispatch begin pointer to content/templates/agents-entry.md (agents:refresh into AGENTS.md) and to the swarm skill through the skills pack.
5. One changelog.d fragment; a content-contract test for the links and the pointer lines.

- AGENTS.md stays within its byte budget.

narratives.Overview:
## Summary

#6295 shipped merge queue mode, and `deftai/directive` master now runs a GitHub merge queue (set 2026-11-16). Nothing tells an agent or a consumer that the queue is available or how to turn it on: the only text is one consumer bullet in `content/scm/github.md` § Merge queue mode. Without the queue, strict "up to date" protection makes every merge put every open PR behind, which cost a rebase, a pre-PR run and a re-review per PR in wave 2a.

## Expected

- A setup playbook, `content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md`, in the shape of `content/docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md`: what the queue is, repository prerequisites (`merge_group` on required workflows, stand-in jobs for app checks, skipped-not-absent required checks), the settings as `gh` commands (auto-merge, required checks with strict off, merge-queue ruleset with an admin bypass for release pushes), verify, how agents merge afterwards, roll back, and this repository's setup as the reference.
- Agents find it where they merge: `content/scm/github.md` § Merge queue mode and the review-cycle skill's merge step point to the playbook.
- `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` on the direct path (no `merge_queue` rule) prints one advisory line naming the playbook when the branch requires strict up-to-date checks. Advisory only: no refusal, no exit-code change.

No new check: this is documentation plus one advisory line.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `content/docs/github-merge-queue-setup.md` exists and covers prerequisites, settings, verify, agent merge behaviour and roll back.
- `content/scm/github.md` § Merge queue mode links the playbook.
- The merge step of `content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` links the playbook.
- Given a branch with strict required checks and no `merge_queue` rule, when `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` runs, then it prints one advisory line naming the playbook and its exit code is unchanged.
- Given a branch with a `merge_queue` rule, when `task pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge` runs, then no advisory line is printed.

Refs #6295.

## Operator scope additions (2026-11-16)

- One pointer in `content/templates/agents-entry.md` (and the refreshed AGENTS.md) and in the swarm skill main SKILL.md: run `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin before starting any implementation worker; it also binds the worktree to its story so the worker's commits are admitted (#6379).
- In the playbook: a short Known issues section (#6423 resume single read; red gate after a release until the pin PR lands; conflict shown as absent-required; #6424 one-pr-unit-merge-group) and a short Saving rounds in the queue section (changelog.d fragments; scope:complete --in-pr, #6277; @slizard label fp, #6377; swarm:pre-dispatch begin, #6379).
